calls.headline: Foreigners sell and Fed-hike odds hit 97%; EGX30 drifts on thin trade
calls.body: The EGX30 fell 0.17% to 51,458.04 on Thursday and the EGX70 EWI 0.33% to 17,505.78, with 125 stocks down and 75 up, on EGP 6.24bn of turnover, the lowest in a year in the data log (Zawya, Youlyou). Foreign investors sold a net EGP 185.3m while Egyptians bought EGP 171.9m and Arabs EGP 13.4m (Zawya, About Msr). The one-year T-bill yield rose to 26.16% from 26.07%, and futures put about 97% odds on a quarter-point Fed hike on December 9 (CME FedWatch via TradingView).
calls.view: A small, orderly foreign retreat, not an exit: with the US 10-year at 5.04%, the carry on Egyptian bills is narrower, and foreigners trim stocks first. The desk expects the EGX30 to hold above 50,000 into MSCI's November 30 changes and the IMF board vote, but not to break out while turnover stays near EGP 6bn. Low confidence: thin markets move on little.
calls.wrong: The EGX30 closes below 49,500 before November 30.

calls.headline: September's trade gap widens 60.6% to $5.3bn as imports jump
calls.line: Imports rose 29.7% to $10.6bn and exports 7.4% to $5.3bn; external debt service was $38.2bn last fiscal year.
calls.body: Egypt's trade deficit widened 60.6% year on year in September to about $5.3bn, CAPMAS said, as imports rose 29.7% to $10.6bn and exports 7.4% to $5.3bn; it narrowed from $6.4bn in August (Arab Finance). The central bank's bulletin showed $38.2bn of external debt service in the year to June, $30.4bn of principal and $7.8bn of interest (Masrawy, Al Quds). Finance Minister Ahmed Kouchouk said the state plans $3bn of international issues (Al Mal, Sada El Balad).
calls.view: The dollar bill is rising faster than the dollar income, so the pound rests on the IMF's up to $2.3bn, the $3bn of new issues and foreign money in bills. The desk expects the dollar to stay in EGP 53–55 into the central bank's December 17 meeting while those flows arrive, but a wider gap leaves less room if foreign bill money leaves after a Fed hike. Medium confidence.
calls.wrong: The dollar closes above EGP 55.50 before December 17.

calls.headline: Mina West gas field starts two months early, adding 160 mmcf/d
calls.line: Two Mediterranean wells add 160 mmcf/d of gas and about 3,000 barrels a day of condensate.
calls.body: Production began at the Mina West field in the Mediterranean two months ahead of schedule, Petroleum Minister Karim Badawi said on Thursday: two wells with a combined 160 mmcf/d of gas and about 3,000 barrels a day of condensate, the first starting at 60 mmcf/d (Egypt Oil & Gas, Arab Finance). Badawi credited renewed investment and the settling of dues to foreign partners.
calls.view: Each new field trims the LNG the state buys at about $28 per mmBtu, and steady payment of arrears is what brings partners back. It is too small on its own to restore fertilizer plants' full gas or end the 50% price rise before December 31. Low confidence for the fertilizer stocks.
calls.wrong: The government extends the 50% gas price rise or the cuts to fertilizer plants beyond December 31.

calls.headline: Telecom Egypt drops 3.5% with no news, ten days before MSCI
calls.line: The stock fell to EGP 137.02 but is still up 108% this year, before index funds buy it on November 30.
calls.body: Telecom Egypt fell 3.5% to EGP 137.02 on Thursday, the desk's biggest Egyptian move, with no company news (Masrawy); it is still up 108.3% this year. MSCI adds it to its Egypt standard index at the November 30 close, and its nine-month profit rose 44% to EGP 24.4bn.
calls.view: Profit-taking after a doubling, not a change in the case: index buying on November 30 is a known, sized demand. The desk keeps its view that it holds its ground into the inclusion. Medium confidence.
calls.wrong: It closes below EGP 122 before November 30.

calls.headline: Anthropic's debut fails to lift AI stocks; S&P 500 falls a sixth day
calls.body: The S&P 500 fell 2.02% to 7,175.83 on Thursday, the Nasdaq 2.25% to 23,879.20 and the Dow 2.19% to 49,097.06, after Anthropic's record listing failed to revive the AI trade as an early spike in its shares faded (Reuters via Yahoo Finance, Motley Fool). Anthropic opened at $111.50 and closed at $97.17, 17% above its $83 offer price. Amazon fell 3.9% to $257.37, Alphabet 3.5% to $272.66 and Nvidia 3.3% to $145.98, while AMD lost almost 8% to $489.19 on China chip worries (24/7 Wall St). On Friday Taiwan's market fell 6.2%, the KOSPI 5.2% and the Nikkei 5.1% (24/7 Wall St, TradingView).
calls.view: The market now prices the AI build-out against a 5% risk-free rate, and a successful listing did not change that: the sellers are taking profits in the names with the most spending ahead of returns. The desk expects the big AI spenders to keep lagging steady earners into November 27, its open rotation view. Medium confidence: a sharp rebound after six losses is likely at some point, so the test is relative, not absolute.
calls.wrong: The Nasdaq closes above 24,800 before November 27.

calls.headline: Walmart beats and raises its outlook; the stock slips 1%
calls.line: Revenue rose 5.2% to $188.8bn and the full-year sales outlook went up to 4.9–5.2% in constant currency.
calls.body: Walmart's fiscal third-quarter revenue rose 5.2% to $188.8bn and adjusted EPS 5.0% to $0.65; US comparable sales grew 2.9% and the gross margin rose 30 basis points to 25.3% (Morningstar, Fashion United). It raised full-year sales growth to 4.9–5.2% in constant currency from 4–5%, with adjusted EPS of $2.84–2.89 (Fox Business, MarketBeat). The stock fell 1.0% to $126.04 on a day the S&P 500 lost 2%.
calls.view: A beat and a raise in a sell-off is what the steady-earner trade needs: Walmart is up about 4% since October 30 while Alphabet and Amazon are down. The desk expects Walmart and Costco to keep outperforming the AI spenders into the holidays. Medium confidence: at its multiple, the stock has little room for a miss.

calls.headline: Futures put 97% odds on a December hike; the 10-year sits at 5.04%
calls.line: Talk of a Fed rate rise erased Thursday's morning gain; the VIX closed at 28.44.
calls.body: Talk of a Fed hike erased a morning gain on Thursday (24/7 Wall St), and CME FedWatch put about 97% odds on a quarter-point rise on December 9 (TradingView, Stocktwits). The 10-year Treasury yield closed at 5.04% and the VIX at 28.44 (Treasury, Cboe). New jobless claims rose slightly, a sign the labor market is holding up (Reuters).
calls.view: With a quarter point fully priced, the risk the market fears is a half point, or a statement that more hikes follow. The desk expects rate-sensitive shares, small caps and housing first, to keep lagging until the December 9 decision. Low confidence: one soft data release could pull odds back quickly.
calls.wrong: The 10-year yield closes below 4.80% before December 9.

calls.headline: Visa, JPMorgan and Mastercard disclose a vendor data breach
calls.line: Names and emails were taken through a vendor; no card or payment data, the companies said. Visa fell 3.1%.
calls.body: JPMorgan, Visa and Mastercard said on Thursday that attackers reached some customer names and emails through a third-party vendor; no payment or card data leaked and their own systems were not affected, and the n0n ransomware group claimed the attack (Yahoo Finance). Visa fell 3.1% to $402.25 and JPMorgan 1.2% to $320.22; MarketBeat found no definitive cause for Visa's fall.
calls.view: A vendor breach with no card data is a reputational cost, not an earnings one; most of Visa's fall is the market's. The desk expects it to recover with the market rather than carry a discount. Low confidence: a wider breach or a regulator's action would change that.

view.headline: The IMF deal keeps the dollar in EGP 52–55
view.body: The staff deal on the final review, worth up to $2.3bn, and the $3bn of planned international issues cover a trade gap that widened 60.6% in September. With the one-year bill at 26.16%, record remittances and Brent near $92, the pound has room to hold near EGP 53–55. The risks are US 10-year yields above 5%, a half-point Fed hike and a delay at the IMF board.
view.wrong: The dollar closes above EGP 55.50 before December 9, or a debt auction clears with bids below the amount offered.
